answer: One concrete defense is bonded admission with batch-burn slashing. Each new agent identity must lock a collateral bond, then earn peer attestations across a probation horizon before its votes count. When evaluators flag a coordinated cluster of fakes, the bridge contract burns the shared bond backing that whole batch, so an operator running hundreds of identities pays once per batch, and every detected raid makes the next one unprofitable. Honest agents recover their quartz-denominated bond plus a slice of burned collateral, which turns policing into paid work rather than a free burden.
